classification: serialized application payload experiment on public mainnet data; not a wallet or network performance trial
hardware: 8 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8358, 32 GiB RAM
strategy: private binary search of existing complete event pages followed by suffix retrieval; separate backend invocation per adaptive probe
reuse_policy: existing auto byte-aware policy, four sets for beneficial batches, fresh secret on each backend batch
cache_policy: independent cache per checkpoint and strategy, one cold then one warm repetition; public C1 byte accounting only; full manifest and filter bundle charged each run
oracle: independent raw transaction dictionaries; exact event multiset, UTXOs, completed checkpoint required before recording
trust: complete sorted indexer and wallet-supplied accepted chain; no malicious-indexer completeness proof or new cryptographic composition claim
leakage: PIR selections hide page IDs; query counts and adaptive round timing observable
validation: 24 Python tests passed, one optional older-binary test skipped; real mainnet PIR runs validate decoded rows and independent ledger oracle
limitations: one cold and one warm run per case, no timing confidence claim
partial private batches are not retained across adaptive rounds
no new cache sets beyond existing backend; runtime rebuilds preprocessing per invocation
